answer: In the agent economy, every participant registers as a unique vertex in a shared atlas of verified identities. Establishing a new vertex requires bonding a quantity of jade, a scarce computational proof token that is locked until the agent completes verifiable tasks. Creating multiple Sybil vertices multiplies the jade cost linearly while the atlas cross-checks interaction patterns against historical graphs, making large-scale fake identity attacks prohibitively expensive as each additional vertex demands independent proof-of-work equivalents that cannot be reused.
